thread:
Maria: Heads-up — we have an open question from sales about how burst credits expire when a customer downgrades mid-cycle. They want a clear, auditable rule for billing + oncall rollback.
Alex: Good catch. Do they mean reserved pool credits or soft burst credits?
Maria: Reserved pool burst credits (the committed monthly headroom). Also edge case: customer cancels mid-cycle + has active prewarm.
Jordan: I think current implementation zeros the remaining credits on churn end date. But that's messy for prewarm and can create surprise billing.
Sam: Yep. We also have internal notes that some customers expect pro-rata refunds or carryover. No refunds today.
Priya: Oncall perspective: if we revoke credits immediately and customer still has active sessions, we need an auto-fallback model + rate-limit to avoid 500s.
ops-bot: Deploy succeeded: release/2661 reserved-credits-txn-log rolled to prod at 11:03 UTC.
Maria: Proposal draft: 1) credits are valid until the *end of the billing cycle* unless explicitly revoked; 2) cancellation triggers a scheduled non-renewal (no prorated refunds); 3) immediate revoke only allowed for fraud/contractual breach and must run through ops.
Alex: Sounds OK. For immediate revoke, add a circuit-breaker: notify oncall, create a temporary spillover pool, and throttle to soft-limit 50% for 10m.
Jordan: We need concrete rollback steps. Example playbook: a) set pool to read-only (no new sessions), b) shift in-flight sessions to fallback model via routing rule, c) drain KV caches and notify customer.
Sam: Can we automate (b) with a routing tag? i.e., set pool.metadata.expire=true and routing-service picks fallback variant.
Priya: +1, but ensure alerting: PagerDuty if more than 5% requests start failing within 2m of revoke.
Maria: Also follow-up: define how prewarm is billed. My suggestion: prewarm is billed as reserved fraction for the remainder of the cycle and stops on revoke. No refunds.
Alex: Edge case: customer downgrades to lower tier mid-cycle but keeps some pool reservations — we should pro-rate the *capacity commitment* forward, not the burst credits. That avoids inconsistent accounting.
Jordan: We need audit logs for every credits state mutation. Current txn log exists (ops-bot message), but create a human-readable changelog entry and customer-visible event in the billing UI.
Sam: Quick check: API call to simulate revoke: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/pools/123/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"expire_at":"now"}'```
Priya: For oncall rollback playbook, draft steps: 1) run revoke -> opaque flag set, 2) push routing tag to fallback models, 3) set throttling policy, 4) kick off billing-notify job, 5) monitor errors & PD. I'll write it up and attach.
Maria: Can someone capture launch criteria for the change? I propose: a) txn logs available and indexed, b) automated fallback routing works end-to-end in staging, c) billing hook emits customer event, d) playbook doc exists and owner assigned.
Alex: I'll own the staging test and verify fallback routing.
Jordan: I'll add the audit + billing event changes to the PR.
Sam: I'll prototype the routing-tag toggle and throttle rule. Priya: I'll draft the oncall playbook and test PD alerts in the dev environment.
Maria: Great — timeline? Prefer shipping before next billing cycle (2w). If blockers surface, we gate on the playbook and PD runbook.
Alex: Will post status updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
Maria: Thanks everyone. If we need legal signoff for no-refund policy, I'll ping @legal next.
Jordan: FYI — related customer case #C-9032 mentions this exact surprise billing; I'll link in the doc.
Sam: Noted.
Priya: Oncall runbook draft link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/dedicated-burst-revoke-playbook (will update).
Maria: Closing action list: Alex (staging test), Jordan (audit + billing event), Sam (routing + throttle), Priya (playbook + PD test). Back here in 48h with updates.
